Phase portrait of a fitted continuous time model

Source: R/ctPhasePortrait.R
ctPhasePortrait.Rd

Draws the model's vector field over a plane of the latent state space, showing at each point the direction and speed in which the deterministic part of the system moves. For a model whose matrices depend on the latent state, this shows behaviour that a single DRIFT matrix cannot describe.

Usage

ctPhasePortrait(
  fit,
  latents = 1:2,
  extent = "data",
  gridsize = 15,
  state = "asymptotic",
  tipreds = NULL,
  nullclines = TRUE,
  fixedpoint = TRUE,
  trajectories = 0,
  plot = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

A ctJuliaFit, or a ctStanFit of a linear model.

latents

Two latent processes, by name or index, forming the plane.

extent

'data' (the default) spans the smoothed latent states, 'sd' spans two stationary standard deviations either side of T0MEANS, or supply a list of two numeric ranges.

gridsize

Arrows per side. Computing time grows with its square.

state

Where the *other* latent processes are held, as in ctDiscretePars: 'asymptotic', 'mean', 'T0MEANS', or a numeric state.

tipreds

Time independent predictor values, or NULL for the population.

nullclines

Draw the curves where each process stops changing?

fixedpoint

Mark the asymptotic state when it is inside the region?

trajectories

Number of subjects' smoothed trajectories to overlay, or 0 for none.

plot

If FALSE, return the field, nullclines and trajectories as data instead of a plot.

Value

A ggplot, or when plot=FALSE a list with field, the latents on the plane, stateLabel naming where the off-plane processes were held, the held process names, and nullclines, fixedpoint and trajectories when asked for. The plot names stateLabel in its subtitle whenever anything is held off-plane.

Details

Three things are drawn over the field, each of which can be turned off:

  • Nullclines, the curves where one process stops changing. Where the nullclines of two processes cross, the whole system is at rest. That is a fixed point, and a nonlinear system may have several.

  • The fixed point found by state='asymptotic', marked when it lies inside the plotted region. Only one fixed point is found, starting from T0MEANS. The nullcline crossings show whether there are others.

  • Smoothed trajectories for a few subjects, so the field can be compared with where the data went.

With more than two latent processes the others are held at state, so the plot shows one slice of the state space, which changes with state.

A linear model has an affine field, straight nullclines and exactly one fixed point. It can be drawn from a stan or a julia fit, but shows nothing beyond the DRIFT matrix. A nonlinear stan fit is refused.

See also

ctContextDependence, ctDiscretePars

Examples

# The arrows show the direction and speed in which the two processes of the
# bundled fit move from each point of the plane. The lines are the
# nullclines, where one process stops changing, and they cross at the fixed
# point. The smoothed trajectories of three subjects are drawn over it.
ctPhasePortrait(ctstantestfit, gridsize = 9, trajectories = 3)

# The same as data: one row of the field per arrow, with its position
# (x, y), direction (dx, dy) and speed, and the fixed point.
pp <- ctPhasePortrait(ctstantestfit, gridsize = 7, plot = FALSE)
head(pp$field)
pp$fixedpoint
